title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 98
paragraphs: Deïokes built these walls around his palace. The rest of the people were ordered to live outside the walls. When the building was complete, he established a protocol—the first of its kind. No one was permitted to enter the king's presence. All business was conducted through messengers. No one could see the king. Laughing or spitting in his presence was forbidden for everyone without exception. He wrapped himself in this ceremony so that his former companions—men raised alongside him, of equally good families and no less courageous—would not grow resentful at seeing him and plot against him. If they could not see him, they might come to think of him as a different kind of being.
